LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm and Pattern Making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm and Pattern Making, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How can a rhythm be created? 2. How are rhythms applied in daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm and Pattern Making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks or signs clearly during critique of

own and others’ rhythms.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner applies the techniques of printing and comes up with unique all-over repeat

pattern patterns.

(PCIs):

• Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during group composition of rhythmic patterns.

• Social Justice: The learner fairly critiques melodies created by others and self.

Link to other learning areas:

• English: The learner applies the concept of syllabic division in reciting French rhythm names of words and writing letters

of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand.

• Mathematics: The learner will use the concept of numbers when relating the value of the quaver in relation to the quaver

and while creating rhythms using note values.

Suggested learning resources:

Open safe quite space, digital devices: laptops, tablets, phones, computers, hearing aids, flash cards with French rhythm

• Integrity: Inculcated as the learner creates own original rhythmic patterns.
